## 3. Ports and adapters (`apps/backend/src/adapters/`)

Adapters grouped by concern; the hexagon direction is adapters → domain ports (AD-1).

- **AI providers** — `adapters/ai-providers/http-provider-adapter.ts` (380) `HttpProviderAdapter implements AiProviderAdapterPort` for `OPENAI` (`$OPENAI_BASE_URL` default `https://api.openai.com/v1`, Bearer), `DEEPINFRA` (default `https://api.deepinfra.com/v1/openai`), `GEMINI` (`.../models/{modelId}:generateContent`, `x-goog-api-key`), `OLLAMA` (default `http://localhost:11434/api/chat`); maps failures to `AiGatewayError` codes. `mock-provider-adapter.ts` `MockProviderAdapter implements AiProviderAdapterPort`. **Port:** `modules/ai/types.ts` `AiProviderAdapterPort`. **Wiring:** `entrypoints/worker.ts:172-178`.
- **Telegram Bot API** — `adapters/telegram/telegram-client.ts` (271, `redactTokenFromUrl`), `telegram-types.ts`. **Port:** `modules/telegram-bot/ports/telegram-client-port.ts` (`TelegramClientPort {validateBot, getChatInfo, verifyMembership, checkPrivacyMode}` + full `TelegramIntegrationError` hierarchy). **Wiring:** `telegram-bot-service.ts` receives a client; note there is no explicit factory binding at a single composition root for this one.
- **MTProto userbot** — `adapters/telegram/userbot-client-adapter.ts` (`GramJsUserbotClient implements UserbotClientPort`, `createDefaultUserbotClientFactory`), `userbot-auth-client.ts` (`GramJsUserbotAuthClient`, `createDefaultUserbotAuthClient`), `mtproto-normalizer.ts` (799, `normalizeMtprotoUpdate`). **Ports:** `modules/userbot/userbot-client-port.ts` (compile-time write-method ban via `_AssertPassiveOnlyPort`), `modules/userbot-session/userbot-auth-port.ts`. **Wiring:** `entrypoints/userbot.ts:48`.
- **Backup verification** — `adapters/backup/system-backup-verifier.ts` (`SystemBackupRetentionVerifier implements BackupRetentionVerifier`, parses pgBackRest), `mock-backup-verifier.ts`. **Port:** `modules/subscriptions/ports/backup-retention-verifier.ts`. **Wiring:** `worker.ts:182-183`, `http.ts` via `options.backupVerifier`.
- **External tombstone store** — `adapters/storage/external-tombstone-store.ts` (`FileExternalTombstoneStore` at `TOMBSTONE_STORE_PATH` || `cwd/deploy/backup/tombstones.json`, atomic tmp+rename; `InMemoryExternalTombstoneStore`). **Port:** `modules/subscriptions/ports/external-tombstone-store.port.ts`. **Wiring:** `reconcile-restore.ts:21`, injected optionally in `http.ts`.
- **Crypto** — `adapters/crypto/`: `argon2.ts`, `password-policy.ts`, `temporary-password.ts` (18-char default, min 15, max 128), `token-cipher.ts` (`encryptToken`/`decryptToken`/`getEncryptionKey`, `FALLBACK_DEV_KEY = 'dev_encryption_key_32_bytes_len!'`, `maskBotToken`), `common-passwords.ts`, `index.ts` (`cryptoService` facade). No port interface — used directly.
- **DB / jobs** — `adapters/db/{client,migrate,seeds}.ts` + 17 schema files; `adapters/jobs/{boss-client,job-types}.ts`.

## 4. Data layer

`apps/backend/drizzle.config.ts` — schema `./src/adapters/db/schema/index.ts`, out `./drizzle`, postgresql, URL fallback `postgresql://mahalla_user:mahalla_dev_password@localhost:5433/mahalla_ovozi`. `adapters/db/migrate.ts` uses advisory lock `MIGRATION_ADVISORY_LOCK_ID = 847291047129481`.

**17 schema modules, 21 tables:** `accounts`, `sessions`, `audit_events`, `sign_in_rate_limits`, `districts`, `district_telegram_bots`, `district_telegram_groups`, `district_telegram_userbot_sessions`, `telegram_intake_records`, `ai_profiles`, `ai_operations`, `ai_provider_attempts`, `district_analysis_settings_versions`, `district_analysis_settings_drafts`, `topics`, `accepted_evidence`, `topic_projections`, `user_dashboard_visits`, `operational_issues`, `district_subscriptions`, `district_deletion_records`.

Key relations: `districts 1─N accounts`; `accounts 1─N sessions`; `districts 1─N district_telegram_bots/groups/subscriptions/deletion_records`; `telegram_intake_records 1─N accepted_evidence`; `topics 1─N accepted_evidence` (ON DELETE **RESTRICT** — comment: "never cascade delete legal civic evidence"); `topics 1─1 topic_projections` (unique `topic_projections_topic_id_idx`); `topic_projections.anchor_evidence_id → accepted_evidence` RESTRICT; `ai_operations` ← `ai_provider_attempts` (unique `(operation_id, attempt_number)`); `ai_profiles` ← `topic_projections.ai_profile_id`.

Notable constraints/indexes: `accounts` role/status/role-district CHECKs + partial unique `accounts_active_district_hokim_idx` on `district_id WHERE role='DISTRICT_HOKIM' AND status='ACTIVE'`; `districts` status CHECK `SETUP_INCOMPLETE|ACTIVE|GRACE|SUSPENDED|CANCELLED` + functional unique `districts_name_lower_idx (LOWER(name))`; `telegram_intake_records` unique `(district_id, telegram_chat_id, telegram_message_id)`; `accepted_evidence` unique `(district_id, telegram_chat_id, telegram_message_id)`; `operational_issues` partial unique `active_logical_key` WHERE status='ACTIVE'; `district_telegram_groups` unique `telegram_chat_id` and unique `(district_id, LOWER(mahalla_name))`.

**28 migrations** `apps/backend/drizzle/0000…0028` + `meta/_journal.json` + snapshots (migrations 0005/0006/0015/0017/0020-0024 have no matching snapshot entries in the observed snapshot list — see risks).

**Tenant/district scoping strategy:** every domain table carries `district_id` (FK → `districts`, `ON DELETE CASCADE`, except the two RESTRICT anchors above); all composite indexes are district-first; enforcement is layered — DB-level (FK + district-first unique indexes), app-level (`createRequireAuth({allowMatchingDistrictOnly})` compares `account.districtId` to `req.params.districtId` at `require-auth.ts:142-153`), and per-service `validateDistrictScope(districtId)` guards (`topic-retention-service.ts:45`, `district-deletion-service.ts:85`). `audit_events.district_id` is nullable (global/admin events); `operational_issues` has a `scope GLOBAL|DISTRICT` CHECK tied to `district_id IS NULL/NOT NULL`.

## 5. Cross-cutting

- **Auth/session:** HttpOnly cookie `mahalla_session` (`session-manager.ts:9`), SHA-256 `token_hash` lookup, 12 h sliding idle + 24 h absolute ceiling (Hokim kiosk renews baseline; Product Owner strictly expires), 60 s touch throttle, `credential_version` invalidation on password change; `revokeAllAccountSessions` for global revocation. Guards: `createRequireAuth` / `createRequireProductOwner` / `createRequireHokim` / `createRequireDistrictAccess`.
- **CSRF/origin:** `verifyStateChangingOrigin` (`origin-guard.ts:40`) fails closed when `Origin` is missing, exempts `/api/v1/telegram/webhook*` and `/api/v1/webhooks/*`. It is applied **selectively** (auth, hokim-topics, district-topics, issue, health, telegram-groups scopes) rather than globally.
- **Zod boundaries:** mixed. 22 route registrations declare Fastify `schema: {}` (validated by `fastify-type-provider-zod` → 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`), but 36 places call `.safeParse()` manually in handlers (`issue-routes` 7, `subscriptions-routes` 6, `telegram-groups-routes` 4, `ai-operations-routes` 3, `district-analysis-settings-routes` 3, `hokim-accounts-routes` 3, `audit-routes` 2, `auth-routes` 2, `districts-routes` 2, others 1 each). Error shape is `{ error: { code, message, statusCode, validationErrors[] } }`.
- **Error handling:** single `setErrorHandler` (`http.ts:154-244`) sanitizes: 5xx messages replaced with the generic Uzbek string, 4xx messages preserved, `blockers`/`details`/`validationErrors` forwarded when present. All user-facing messages are Uzbek.
- **Logging:** two mechanisms — Fastify's Pino logger for HTTP (`http.ts:96-104`), and a hand-rolled JSON `logger` in `src/utils/logger.ts` (stdout for debug/info, stderr for warn/error, silenced under `NODE_ENV=test` unless `TEST_LOGS`). They do not share configuration.
- **Audit:** `recordAuditEvent()` writes to `audit_events` with `id = aud_<uuid>`; `sanitizeMetadata()` recursively drops a `SENSITIVE_KEYS` blocklist and regex-redacts bot tokens, `sk-*`, `AIza*`, `Bearer …`; `classifyAuditActionCategory()` buckets actions by prefix. Audit write is a plain insert — **it is not enforced to run inside the caller's transaction** by the helper signature (`db: DbOrTx`, so callers can pass `tx`).
- **Background jobs:** 13 queues, typed payload registry `BossQueueMap` (`job-types.ts:207`). Cron (all UTC): `telegram-topic-projection-reconcile-cron` `*/2 * * * *` (`topic-projection-job-handler.ts:454`), `district-live-deletion-cron` `* * * * *` (`district-deletion-job-handler.ts:202`), `district-backup-expiry-cron` `*/5 * * * *` (:225), `district-subscription-expiry-cron` `* * * * *` (`subscription-expiry-job-handler.ts:53`). Dedup via `JobSingletonKeys`. `withTransactionalIntake()` (`boss-client.ts:222`) enqueues jobs inside the same Postgres transaction as the domain write using `boss.send(..., {db:{executeSql}})` bound to the checked-out client. Per-queue resilience configs in `DEFAULT_QUEUE_CONFIGS` (retryLimit 2-5, backoff, expire 10-30 min, retention 1-3 days).

- `apps/backend/vitest.config.ts` — `fileParallelism: false` (serial), `testTimeout: 20000`, env `DATABASE_URL=…/mahalla_ovozi_test` and `AI_PROVIDER=OLLAMA`. No `setupFiles`/`globalSetup`.
- `apps/backend/tests/` — 85 `*.test.ts` files (~28 k lines), plus `tests/helpers/mock-ai-gateway.ts` and `tests/unit/` (3 files).
- **Test-DB assumption:** ~40+ suites reference `DATABASE_URL` / `createDbPool` / `runMigrations`, i.e. they are real-Postgres integration tests against `mahalla_ovozi_test` — the suite cannot run without a live Postgres on `localhost:5433`. `fileParallelism: false` is consistent with shared-DB truncation between tests.

## 7. Observed risks, smells, unclear areas

**Risks / smells (observed, not speculated):**
1. **Config mismatch between deploy and code.** `deploy/compose/.env.example:12-14` advertises `AI_PROVIDER=GROQ` + `AI_MODEL_ID=llama-3.3-70b-versatile` + `GROQ_API_KEY`, but `HttpProviderAdapter` supports only `OPENAI|GEMINI|DEEPINFRA|OLLAMA` and `AiGateway.getAdapter` throws `PROVIDER_SERVER_ERROR: No adapter registered for AI provider: <x>`. Following the example env file verbatim would break every AI job.
2. **Three disagreeing AI defaults.** `modules/ai/ai-config.ts:16-19` hardcodes `DEEPINFRA` + `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`; `adapters/db/seeds.ts:13-27` falls back to `OLLAMA`/`gemma4:12b`; `vitest.config.ts:9` forces `AI_PROVIDER=OLLAMA`. The effective provider depends on both `AI_PROVIDER` and `AI_MODEL_ID` being set.
3. **Inconsistent validation boundary.** Two validation idioms coexist (route-level Fastify `schema` vs. in-handler `.safeParse()`), with the majority being manual. Only the route-level path gets the `hasZodFastifySchemaValidationErrors` branch; manual `safeParse` failures are shaped per handler, so error payloads for the same class of error are not uniform.
4. **CSRF guard applied selectively.** `verifyStateChangingOrigin` is registered on some scopes but not all mutating scopes (e.g. it is absent from `districts-routes.ts`, `subscriptions-routes.ts`, `hokim-accounts-routes.ts`, `telegram-bot-routes.ts`, `userbot-session-routes.ts`, `ai-operations-routes.ts`, `audit-routes.ts` per the observed `addHook` matches). Note it does **not** exclude `docs/`, `apps/backend/tests/`, or `apps/web/tests/` — the builder stage therefore copies tests and docs into the image layer that `runner` inherits via `COPY --from=builder /app /app`.
- `.gitignore`: `node_modules/`, `.pnpm-store/`, `dist/`, `build/`, `.output/`, `*.tsbuildinfo`, `logs/`, `*.log`, npm/pnpm/yarn debug logs, `.env`, `.env.*`, `!.env.example`, `.DS_Store`, `Thumbs.db`, `.idea/`, `.vscode/`, `*.swp`, `*.swo`, `coverage/`, `.nyc_output/`, `playwright-report/`, `test-results/`, `blob-report/`, `.grepai/`, `.temp/`, `.tmp/`, `tombstones.json`, `**/tombstones.json`. The `tombstones.json` rules correctly keep the privacy-sensitive deletion-proof file out of version control — and `pnpm-lock.yaml` is correctly **not** ignored.

---

## 4. Cross-cutting observations (linking to the t1/t2 app summaries)

**Where contracts are actually consumed.** `@mahalla-ovozi/api-contracts` has **57 import sites in `apps/backend/src`** and **96 in `apps/web/src`** (recursive content search over `.ts`/`.tsx`). This matches the t1 finding that the backend's Zod boundary is mixed (22 Fastify `schema:{}` registrations + 36 manual `.safeParse()` calls) and the t2 finding that the web app's hooks/clients are the primary consumers. In the web tree the importers are concentrated in `api-client.ts`, per-domain clients (`telegram-bot-client.ts`, `telegram-group-client.ts`), and `use*` hooks (`useDistrictActivation`, `useDistrictAnalysisSettings`, `useDistrictReadiness`, `useDistrictWorkspace`, `useHokimAccount`, `useHokimTopicBoard`, …) plus page components (`SubscriptionsPage.tsx`, `SystemHealthPage.tsx`) and tables/drawers. So the shared package is genuinely load-bearing on both sides — not a decorative layer.

**Contract ⟷ DB constraint duplication is intentional and currently consistent.** The lifecycle enums in api-contracts mirror the CHECK constraints in `apps/backend/src/adapters/db/schema/*.ts` exactly: `TelegramGroupStatusSchema = ['PENDING','TESTING','VALID','FAILED']` ↔ `district_telegram_groups_status_check`; `LiveDeletionStatusEnumSchema = ['COMPLETED','FAILED']` ↔ `district_deletion_records_live_deletion_status_check`; `BackupExpiryStatusEnumSchema = ['PENDING','VERIFIED','FAILED']` ↔ `..._backup_expiry_status_check`; `RestoreReconciliationStatusEnumSchema = ['PENDING','RECONCILED','FAILED']` ↔ `..._restore_reconciliation_status_check`. Three parallel sources of truth (Zod, Drizzle CHECK, SQL migration) — consistent today, with no automated check that they stay so.

**Docker Compose duplication.** `docker-compose.yml` (root) and `deploy/compose/docker-compose.yml` both define the `postgres` service with identical image/ports/volume/healthcheck. The root file is the one wired to `pnpm db:up` / `pnpm db:down`, so the `userbot` dev service that exists only in `deploy/compose/docker-compose.yml` is **not** started by any documented root script.

**Postgres major-version drift.** Dev (`docker-compose.yml` L3, `deploy/compose/docker-compose.yml` L3) and CI (`ci.yml` L19) all use `postgres:18-alpine`; production (`docker-compose.prod.yml` L3) uses `postgres:16-alpine`. Dev/CI therefore exercise a newer major than production runs, and `pgBackRest` in the runner image is paired with PG 16.

**API-provider env drift (carried over from t1).** `deploy/compose/.env.example` advertises `AI_PROVIDER=GROQ` + `GROQ_API_KEY`; the real backend env file uses `AI_PROVIDER` + `DEEPINFRA_*` + `OLLAMA_BASE_URL`. The backend's `HttpProviderAdapter` and `AiGateway` support only `OPENAI|GEMINI|DEEPINFRA|OLLAMA`. There is no `GROQ` code path anywhere — the example file is stale.

**Two independent DB-name/port conventions.** Local dev and tests use port `5433` and database `mahalla_ovozi` / `mahalla_ovozi_test` (`deploy/compose/docker-compose.yml:11`, `apps/backend/vitest.config.ts:8`, `apps/backend/drizzle.config.ts:8`). Inside compose the app connects to `postgres:5432` (`docker-compose.prod.yml:37`). CI uses `localhost:5432`. Consistent per-environment, but there are three different authorities for the connection string (compose env, drizzle.config default, vitest env).

**`pnpm build` is not what production runs.** The `builder` stage compiles contracts + SPA with `tsc`/`vite` (Dockerfile L24-25), but every runtime entry point (`Dockerfile:45`, `docker-compose.prod.yml:62`, `:92`) executes `node --import tsx/esm src/entrypoints/*.ts`. The TypeScript backend is transpiled on every container start rather than shipped pre-compiled, and the `api-contracts` `dist/` emitted in the builder is unused because the exports map points at `src/`.

**Prod compose declares `build:` but the documented deploy is `pull`.** `deploy/compose/docker-compose.prod.yml` builds all four app services from `../..` with the local `Dockerfile`, while `deploy/README.md:61` instructs `docker compose pull && docker compose up -d`. Without a registry-backed `image:` on those services, `pull` has nothing to fetch and `up -d` will build on the VPS.

---

## 5. Risks & unclear areas actually observed

### Risks / smells

**R1 — DR runbook step 1 references a file that does not exist.** `deploy/backup/runbook.md:28` runs `caddy reload --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile.maintenance`, and `deploy/compose/Caddyfile.maintenance` is **absent** from the repo (verified). The very first step of the disaster-recovery procedure cannot execute as written.

**R2 — DR runbook step 3 references a service that is not defined.** `deploy/backup/runbook.md:44` runs `docker compose run --rm pgbackrest pgbackrest --stanza=mahalla_ovozi --delta restore`, but no `pgbackrest` service exists in `deploy/compose/docker-compose.prod.yml` (verified by searching the file and the whole `deploy/` tree). `pgbackrest` is only installed as an OS package in the `runner` image (`Dockerfile:32`). Restore cannot proceed as documented.

**R3 — Stale AI provider advertised.** `deploy/compose/.env.example:12-14` offers `AI_PROVIDER=GROQ` / `AI_MODEL_ID=llama-3.3-70b-versatile` / `GROQ_API_KEY`; no GROQ adapter exists. An operator following the example file breaks every AI job with `PROVIDER_SERVER_ERROR: No adapter registered for AI provider: GROQ`.

**R4 — Postgres major-version skew between prod and everything else.** Prod `postgres:16-alpine` vs dev/CI `postgres:18-alpine` (`docker-compose.prod.yml:3`; `docker-compose.yml:3`; `deploy/compose/docker-compose.yml:3`; `ci.yml:19`).

**R5 — `api-contracts` publishes source, not build output.** `package.json` `main`/`types` point at `./dist/*` while the `exports` map resolves `.` to `./src/index.ts` (L9-14). Consumers compile TS directly; the committed `dist/` (26 files) is orphaned and can silently go stale relative to `src/`. Any tool that honours `main` instead of `exports` would load a different artifact than the one being tested.

**R6 — `pull`-based deploy instructions against `build:`-based compose.** See §4. No `image:` key exists on `backend`/`worker`/`userbot`/`caddy`, so `docker compose pull` per `deploy/README.md:61` is a no-op and the documented "zero downtime" deploy will instead rebuild on the VPS.

**R7 — Empty `scripts/` directory at repo root.** The directory exists with 0 entries while `apps/web/scripts/` holds the real script. Empty directories are not tracked by git, so this is either a local artifact or a placeholder; either way it is misleading given `package.json` has no root-level script file.

**R8 — Committed SSH test logs at repo root.** `test_ssh.log` and `test_ssh_vvv.log` are present as untracked/working-tree files at the repo root. `.gitignore` covers `*.log` so they are not committed, but they are sitting in the project root of a repo whose `deploy/README.md` documents a passwordless SSH identity file.

**R9 — Worker and userbot have no healthchecks.** `docker-compose.prod.yml` gives `postgres` and `backend` healthchecks but none for `worker` (L55-83) or `userbot` (L85-108), despite both being `restart: unless-stopped` and both *depending* on `backend: service_healthy`. A wedged queue consumer or a silently disconnected MTProto session is invisible to compose.

**R10 — Runbook mixes execution contexts.** Steps 1-3, 5, 6 are `docker compose` commands on the VPS, but step 4 is `pnpm reconcile-restore` — a host-side workspace command. From a local machine that is not the same host as the VPS, and from the VPS itself it requires a checkout plus a pnpm toolchain that the runner image (which is what the runbook otherwise operates in) does not expose. The `deploy/README.md` command set does not cover this.

**R11 — Hardcoded production IP in two files.** `deploy/compose/Caddyfile:43` (`http://95.182.118.3`) and `deploy/README.md:19` (`HostName 95.182.118.3`). Changing hosts requires editing committed files, and the Caddy redirect only exists for that one literal address.

**R12 — `@types/node` catalog pin is behind the engine floor.** Catalog `@types/node: ^22.13.9` (`pnpm-workspace.yaml:10`) while `engines.node: ">=24.0.0"` and CI/Docker both use Node 24. Backend and web both consume `@types/node: "catalog:"`.

**R13 — `runner` image ships tests and docs.** `.dockerignore` excludes `dist`, `node_modules`, `.git`, `.agents`, `.grepai` and env files but **not** `apps/backend/tests/` (~28 000 lines, 85 suites), `apps/web/tests/`, or `docs/`; `Dockerfile:36` copies the whole `/app` from `builder`. Production image carries the entire test corpus and internal docs.

**R14 — Three parallel sources of truth for lifecycle enums.** Zod schemas (api-contracts), Drizzle `check()` definitions, and raw SQL in `apps/backend/drizzle/*.sql`. They agree today by discipline only; nothing in CI cross-checks them.

**R15 — Runtime never uses the compiled backend.** All three entry points run `tsx/esm` against `src/` (`Dockerfile:45`, `docker-compose.prod.yml:62`, `:92`), so production executes TypeScript transpiled at container start, and the `builder` stage's `tsc` output for the backend is not what runs. `apps/backend/package.json:9` typechecks but only `main: ./dist/entrypoints/http.js` (L6) implies a compiled path that nothing invokes.

**R16 — Doc/code path mismatch for audit history.** `deploy/backup/runbook.md:112` cites `/api/v1/audit/history`; the backend registers `GET /api/v1/audit/events` and `GET /api/v1/audit/events/:id` (`apps/backend/src/modules/audit/audit-routes.ts:24,60`). No `/api/v1/audit/history` route exists.

**R17 — Machine-specific paths in committed config.** `.agents/mcp_config.json` hardcodes `C:/Users/Zubaydulla/AppData/Local/Programs/grepai/grepai.exe` and the absolute repo path; `.grepai/config.yaml:28` stores a `last_index_time` timestamp; `.grepai/` also contains stale `index.gob.tmp-*` / `*.lock` files. None of this is portable to a second machine.

**R18 — `userbot` lacks the tombstone mount and `TOMBSTONE_STORE_PATH`.** `backend` and `worker` mount `../backup:/app/deploy/backup` and set `TOMBSTONE_STORE_PATH=/app/deploy/backup/tombstones.json` (`docker-compose.prod.yml:38-40, 74-76`); `userbot` sets neither (L100-103). If any userbot path ever touches tombstones it would resolve the default relative path inside the container instead.

**R19 — Default tombstone path is cwd-dependent.** `FileExternalTombstoneStore` falls back to `path.resolve(process.cwd(), 'deploy/backup/tombstones.json')` (t1 finding). Running the backend with cwd=`apps/backend` resolves to `apps/backend/deploy/backup/tombstones.json`, which is exactly where a `tombstones.json` was observed in the working tree — a different file from the `deploy/backup/tombstones.json` the prod compose and the DR runbook assume. Both are `.gitignore`d (`tombstones.json`, `**/tombstones.json`), so the divergence is invisible in version control.

### Unclear / not verified (stated explicitly — not guessed)
- I did **not** read any env *values*; only variable names. Whether `apps/backend/.env` and `deploy/compose/.env` are internally consistent with each other cannot be asserted.
- I did **not** read `docs/adr/0008-single-host-compose-caddy-edge.md` or `docs/adr/0009-userbot-transport-abstraction-and-accepted-risks.md` in full, so I cannot confirm whether R6 (pull vs build) and the userbot risk posture are already covered by an accepted decision. The ADR titles alone suggest 0008 and 0009 are the relevant ones.
- I did **not** execute `docker compose config`, so I cannot confirm that the prod compose file parses cleanly with a real `.env` present, nor that `caddy` → `backend` proxying resolves on `mahalla-net` at runtime.
- `apps/web/scripts/check-bundle-budgets.js` (56 lines) was not read; whether it is wired into CI is not determinable from `ci.yml` (no `check:budgets` step appears there).
- The relationship between the ~50 `.agents/skills/` directories and the 40 entries in `skills-lock.json` was compared by name only; I did not verify the `computedHash` values.
- No check was run for whether `.grepai/index.gob` is stale relative to the working tree, nor whether `pnpm-lock.yaml` is in sync with the manifests.
- Whether the VPS actually hosts a registry, and whether `docker compose pull` in `deploy/README.md` predates the switch to `build:` in the prod compose file, cannot be determined from the repository alone.

**Method note:** strictly read-only. No file was created, edited or deleted; no docker, ssh, migration, build or server command was executed. All line numbers come from `read`/`grep`/`Select-String` output on the working tree at reconnaissance time.

# t4 [wave2-docs-architecture] — Architecture Decisions, Domain Model, Specs, Repo Governance (read-only)

No file was created, edited, or deleted; nothing was executed. All claims below come from direct reads/greps of the working tree. Doc paths are workspace-relative.

---

## 1. Domain model — `CONTEXT.md` (58 lines)

Purpose (L3): "cautious, evidence-backed situational awareness for District Hokims by synthesizing public signals from authorized Telegram groups into structured daily topics... leaving every real-world decision and response entirely to human leadership."

Explicit **non-goals** (L7-10): not a citizen complaint portal / petition system / public CRM ("Citizens are evidence sources, not application users"); not a case-management/ticketing system (no resolution tracking, no department task assignment); not an automated decision-maker or verified truth engine.

Canonical vocabulary (term → product UI label → stated avoid-synonyms):

| Term | UI label | _Avoid_ (L ref) |
|---|---|---|
| District | *Tuman* | Tenant, workspace, organization, account, city (L16) |
| Mahalla | *Mahalla* | Neighborhood, borough, zone, precinct (L20) |
| Hokim | *Hokim* | Mayor, governor, admin, client, user, operator (L24) |
| Product Owner | *Mahsulot egasi* | Superadmin, developer, staff, system administrator (L28) |
| Accepted Evidence | *Qabul qilingan dalil* | Message, chat, complaint, ticket, citizen report, grievance, incident (L32) |
| Topic | *Mavzu* | Issue, ticket, thread, incident, story, task, case, multi-day problem (L36) |
| Lane | *Yo'nalish* | Category, bucket, tag, column, board, department (L40) |
| Signal | — | Complaint, emergency, verified fact, petition, grievance (L44) |
| Audit Record | *Audit yozuvi* | Activity log, event stream, access log (L48) |

Key semantic constraints: District is "one isolated customer deployment for one Hokim" owning its own bots/groups/mahallas/topics/audit/subscription state (L14-15); Hokim is "the primary reader... and holds **zero administrative privileges** over the application" (L23); Accepted Evidence is "preserved **verbatim**" and has passed noise filtering + structural sanity checks + semantic relevance analysis (L31); Topic is "strictly bound to a single calendar day (00:00:00 to 23:59:59 `Asia/Tashkent`) and never rolls over across days" (L35); one Topic "may project into multiple relevant Lanes" (L39); Audit Record is "append-only, immutable... without ever storing raw resident evidence or secrets" (L47).

### Technical invariants (L52-57) restated as checkable rules
1. **Monorepo** — pnpm 10.x workspaces, strict TypeScript 5.x ESM; `package.json` + `pnpm-lock.yaml` are the sole version authority. *Check:* no dependency version is declared outside a manifest/lockfile; no CommonJS entry.
2. **Backend shape** — Fastify 5.x API and pg-boss worker run from the same codebase image; domain code lives under `apps/backend/src/modules/`, external systems behind `adapters/`. *Check:* every adapter is imported by modules only through a port; no pg-boss/Telegram/AI SDK import inside `modules/` core logic.
3. **Frontend shape** — React 19.x SPA, Vite 6.x, react-router-dom v7; Ant Design 5.x with design tokens; TanStack Query 5.x owns server state. *Check:* no server data cached in component state/Redux; theme values come from tokens.
4. **Contracts** — `@mahalla-ovozi/api-contracts` holds browser-safe Zod request/response schemas; DB rows and provider SDK objects never cross the API boundary. *Check:* no Drizzle row type or vendor SDK type appears in a route response signature.
5. **Time** — timestamps stored as PostgreSQL `timestamptz` in UTC; product calendar days and user-facing time derived strictly in `Asia/Tashkent`. *Check:* no naive/local-time storage; every day-boundary computation passes through a Tashkent helper.
6. **Testing isolation** — all automated tests touching PostgreSQL or queues run strictly against `mahalla_ovozi_test`, never `mahalla_ovozi`. *Check:* no test config references the dev DB name.
7. **Deployment** — single-host Docker Compose on a domestic Linux VPS via Airnet.uz (Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, BKM datacenter, Tashkent) for TAS-IX/UZ-IX latency and national data sovereignty. *Check:* no multi-host orchestrator, no foreign managed data store.

---

## 2. `docs/adr/` — ADR 0001-0009, all `status: accepted`

Each entry: decision + why (rejected alternatives) + code verdict from wave-1 evidence.

### 5.4 `.agents/rules/grepai.md` (66 lines)
`grepai` is the primary tool for semantic exploration and call-graph tracing. Routing table: intent/domain logic → `grepai search` (semantic embeddings); callers/callees/graphs before edits → `grepai trace` (AST-aware); exact literals (imports, names, configs) → `grep_search`/ripgrep; path patterns → `find_by_name`/fd. **Always** pass `--json` for structured AI consumption and `--compact` on searches (~80% token savings). Queries must be in **English** (embeddings are English-dominant), describe intent not implementation, and be specific. Standard workflow: search → trace → read specific files via `view_file` with grepai's line numbers → ripgrep only for literal verification. Fallback on "no workspaces configured": retry without the workspace param, check the local `.grepai/` index/status, and only then fall back to standard grep/find.

## 6. Synthesis

**What this system is.** Mahalla Ovozi is a **multi-tenant civic situational-awareness platform** for Uzbekistan's district administrations. Telegram messages from authorized Mahalla groups are ingested, noise-filtered, semantically qualified, and clustered by an LLM into same-day **Topics** projected onto a 5-**Lane** executive dashboard (Water, Electricity, Gas, Waste, Hokim-related) that a **Hokim** reads each morning. A separate **Product Owner Console** manages Districts, bots, subscriptions, Hokim accounts, AI operations, and audit history. It is explicitly **not** a complaint/ticketing system and makes no decisions — it is a briefing tool with a human always in the loop (CONTEXT.md:3, L7-10).

**Architectural style.** A **hexagonal modular monolith** on a **single-host Compose edge**. One codebase, four process entrypoints (`http`, `worker`, `userbot`, `reconcile-restore`) sharing `src/`; domain modules behind ports, infrastructure in adapters; PostgreSQL is simultaneously the system of record, the queue (pg-boss), the session store, and the AI-profile store; Caddy terminates TLS and serves the SPA; everything runs on one Airnet.uz VPS for data sovereignty. The only deliberate seam between two runtimes is the userbot transport, isolated as its own container because MTProto sockets are ban-prone and crash-prone.

**The 8 facts a new engineer must know:**
1. **Tenant isolation is explicit, not ambient** (ADR-0006) — every District-scoped query/mutation/job takes a `district_id`, and a missing scope must fail loudly. There is no RLS safety net.
2. **PostgreSQL is the queue** (ADR-0002) — intake and job enqueue happen in one transaction via `withTransactionalIntake` (`apps/backend/src/adapters/jobs/boss-client.ts:222`). There is no Redis/RabbitMQ. DB connection pressure is the scaling limit.
3. **A Topic can never span midnight** (ADR-0003) — same-day `Asia/Tashkent` boundaries, immutable per-day records. An overnight outage becomes two Topics.
4. **Contracts are Zod, and they are validated twice** — server-side via fastify-type-provider-zod, client-side on every response in `apps/web/src/lib/api-client.ts`. DB rows and provider SDK objects never cross the boundary (CONTEXT.md:55).
5. **AI is provider-neutral and versioned** (ADR-0005) — model choice is DB config (`ai_profiles`), not code; a config change mints a new immutable profile so historical runs keep their lineage.
6. **Sessions are stateful by design** (ADR-0007) — suspending or cancelling a District must kill Hokim access instantly, which is why JWT was rejected.
7. **There are two transports, one pipeline** (ADR-0009) — `BOT_API` (default) and `USERBOT` (opt-in MTProto) converge on the same transactional core and dedup key; the userbot port is compile-time guarded to be passive-only (`apps/backend/src/modules/userbot/userbot-client-port.ts:27,47`) and carries accepted ToS/ban/consent risks.
8. **Documentation is code-adjacent and partly load-bearing** — `CONTEXT.md` is the vocabulary authority and `docs/adr/` the invariant authority (AGENTS.md:5-6), so drift between them and the code is a real defect, not a cosmetic one. See Risk 1.
